title: Lanes, Positioning & Lane Changes
whatItIs: Keep left unless overtaking or turning right, follow lane signs and markings, and change lanes with MSM without forcing anyone to change course or speed.
keyFacts: Keep left unless signs or markings say otherwise, or you're overtaking, turning right or passing an obstruction.
To change lane: mirrors, a quick sideways glance if needed, signal, and move only when it's clear.
Give way to cyclists when changing direction or lane: don't cut across them, including in cycle lanes.

keyFacts.text: You MUST NOT drive or park in a cycle lane marked by a solid white line during its times of operation.

keyFacts: In congested traffic don't change lanes unnecessarily. Merging in turn is only for very low speeds.

keyFacts.text: In a one-way street, traffic MUST travel in the direction shown by the signs.

visual.caption: Which lane to use (Highway Code rules 135–139 and 143)

rows: Stay in the left lane; right lane to overtake or turn right
Middle or right lanes to overtake, then back to the middle and the left
Middle lane only to overtake or turn right; never the right lane
Only the lanes that signs or markings show
Left lane to go left, right lane to go right, best lane ahead
Use it if you are slow or others want to overtake
notes: Signs and road markings take priority over these general rules.

a.label: Cycle lane: solid white line
points: You MUST NOT drive or park in it during its times of operation
Times are shown on the signs

b.label: Cycle lane: broken white line
points: Don't drive or park in it unless it's unavoidable
Advice, not a MUST: but still give way to cyclists

onTheTest.question: On a three-lane single carriageway with no priority markings, how should your pupil use the middle lane?
options: Only for overtaking or turning right
Only when traffic in their direction is heavy
Never: it is reserved for emergency vehicles
onTheTest.why: Rule 135: use the middle lane only for overtaking or turning right. You have no more right to it than a driver coming the other way, and don't use the right-hand lane.

onTheTest.question: After passing a lorry on a two-lane dual carriageway, a candidate stays in the right lane with the left lane clear. Where does DT1 record this?
onTheTest.why: Rule 137: after overtaking, move back to the left-hand lane when it's safe. DT1 section 12 lists driving in the right-hand lane of a dual carriageway under Positioning: normal driving.

traps: Where lanes are marked, keep to the middle of your lane: straddling lane markings is a lane discipline fault.
In slow-moving traffic, don't change to a lane on your left to overtake.
A bus or cycle lane outside its hours can be used: DT1 records not using it when allowed as a positioning fault.
Keep well to the left on right-hand bends: a better view and less risk from oncoming traffic.
